title: Session switchback latency/cost field notes
content:
Purpose:
Capture quick experimental notes for the "session switchback" pattern: frequent short-lived session flips (A->B->A) that exercise KV cache thrash and routing fallbacks. Goal is to compare latency and incremental per-query cost across three runtime presets and two model packing modes. This is a rapid field writeup (notes to self + action items).

Summary (top-line):
- Switchback pattern increases p95 by 1.4-2.5x depending on cache policy.
- Cost per query rises modestly when kv-hitrate < 40% due to additional kernel work and context reloads.
- Prefetching small prefixes reduces p50 by ~8% but can increase p99 if cold-starts become correlated.

Experiment matrix (configs):
- Workload: synthetic session stream derived from PROD-sample-042 (avg turn len 42 tokens, bursty inter-arrival, mean 3 turns/session).
- Runtimes: fastpath (low-latency, small-batch), multiplex (higher packing), tiling (slotized long-lived).
- KV/cache modes: aggressive-prefetch, lazy-kv (no prefetch), sticky-kv (session-affinity pinned cache).
- Model packing: full-weights (FP16), 4-bit-quant (Q4).

Quick ascii table: median latency (ms) | p95 latency (ms) | est $/k tokens
-----------------------------------------------------------------
fastpath + aggressive-prefetch + FP16  :  82  |  210  |  $6.2  
fastpath + lazy-kv + FP16              :  95  |  275  |  $7.0  
multiplex + sticky-kv + FP16           :  120 |  320  |  $5.8  
multiplex + lazy-kv + Q4               :  140 |  410  |  $4.1  
tiling + sticky-kv + Q4                 :  160 |  460  |  $3.9  

Observations and interpretation:
- Fastpath with aggressive prefetch wins for p50/p90 but is brittle: when sessions flip cold, p99 spikes dramatically (seen in tail samples). That suggests prefetch amplifies correlated cold penalties.
- Multiplex (packing) shows better amortized $/k tokens for mixed Q4 workloads because longer decode amortization outweighs slightly higher median latency.
- Tiling gives stable cost at scale but higher base latency (expected). In switchback scenario, tiling's session affinity helps; sticky-kv kept p95 lower than lazy-kv when session stickiness holds.

ASCII sparkline of p95 across time for three configs (sample window 30m, normalized):
Time -> 00 05 10 15 20 25 30 (minutes)
fastpath-prefetch:  ▁▂▃▇▇▇▂▁  (spike cluster at 10-20m)
multiplex-sticky  :  ▂▃▅▆▅▃▂▂  (smoother tail)
tiling-sticky     :  ▁▁▂▃▃▃▂▁  (most stable)

Micro anecdotes from logs (snippets):
- 2026-03-28T09:12:33Z session=abc123 route=fastpath prefetch=true kv_miss=true fallback=multiplex latency_ms=398 p99
- 2026-03-28T09:18:02Z session=def456 route=multiplex sticky_kv=true kv_miss=false latency_ms=128 p95
- 2026-03-28T09:20:41Z session=ghi789 route=tiling sticky_kv=true packing_slot=slot-7 latency_ms=172

Small cost breakdown (rough math):
- Extra token cost when kv_miss: ~+0.3ms/token compute equivalent, plus memory page load overhead.
- Prefetch warmed 20% of following-turn tokens on average; savings appear when turn length > 20 tokens.

Open questions / confounding factors:
1) Synthetic sampling might underrepresent inter-session correlation seen in real traffic — need a replay run against RPS=prod*0.6.
2) Autoscaler interaction: tiling kept affinity but may delay slot reclamation; what is long-term cost when idle churn increases?
3) Network jitter contribution to p99 in fastpath — need to separate kernel queuing vs network tail via trace IDs.

Next steps / action items (short):
- [ ] Run 2h replay on canary with real traffic subset (INF-4821) — schedule with platform on Thu 2026-03-31. (Owner: Ava)
- [ ] Add p99 decomposition traces for fastpath flows (tracepoints: cache-load-start, cache-load-done, kernel-queue-enter) (Owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Evaluate hybrid prefetch (prefetch small prefix only when session-turns > 2) across multiplex and fastpath (Owner: Lena)
- [ ] Postmortem checklist item: add guardrail that disables aggressive-prefetch for routes with >30% correlated cold starts (followup PR needed)

Notes to self / heuristics learned: keep an eye on "switchback density" (fraction of sessions that flip within 30s). When density > 0.25, sticky-kv + packing beats eager prefetch in tail cost.

  ./benchrunner --profile switchback --seed 20260328 --rps 1200 --turn-len-mean 42 --flip-window 30s --out /tmp/switchback-03-28.log
